title: Pips and pipettes

inOneLine.simple: A pip is the usual small step in a currency price. A pipette is one tenth of a pip.
inOneLine.balanced: Price moves are counted in [[pip|pips]]: 0.0001 for most pairs and 0.01 for most yen pairs. The extra digit many platforms show is a [[pipette]].

explain.simple: Traders count price moves in pips. For most pairs, like EUR/USD, one pip is 0.0001, the fourth digit after the dot. For pairs with the Japanese yen, like USD/JPY, one pip is 0.01, the second digit after the dot. Many platforms show one more digit than that. That last digit is a pipette. Ten pipettes make one pip.
explain.balanced: A 5-digit quote such as 1.10253 has a pip in the fourth decimal and a [[pipette]] in the fifth. A 3-digit yen quote such as 150.253 has a pip in the second decimal and a pipette in the third. MetaTrader often calls a pipette a 'point', so a distance of 50 points on a 5-digit pair is only 5 pips. Always check whether a number is in pips or points.

assumptions: Illustrative prices, not live market data

explainSimpler: A pip is like one centimetre on a ruler for price. Most pairs use the fourth digit after the dot. Yen pairs use the second.
commonMistake: Treating the last digit on the screen as a pip. On a 5-digit quote the last digit is a pipette, so a 30-point move is only 3 pips. Yen pairs are another trap: using 0.0001 for USD/JPY makes your pip count 100 times too big.

quickCheck.prompt: EUR/USD moves from 1.2000 to 1.2025. How many pips is that?

options.explanation: No: 250 pips would be a move of 0.0250.

quickCheck.prompt: USD/JPY moves from 148.20 to 148.50. How many pips is that?

options.explanation: Right: for yen pairs a pip is 0.01, and 0.30 ÷ 0.01 = 30 pips.
No: that uses 0.0001 as the pip, which is wrong for yen pairs.
No: 3 pips on a yen pair would be a move of 0.03.

quickCheck.prompt: On a 5-digit EUR/USD quote, how many pipettes make one pip?

options.explanation: Right: a pipette is one tenth of a pip.
No: a pipette is smaller than a pip, not the same size.

doItNow.instructions: Pick three pairs, including one yen pair. For each one, write down two made-up prices and work out the move in pips and in pipettes. Check the yen pair uses 0.01 per pip.

homework: In MetaTrader on your demo account, note the price of EUR/USD and USD/JPY now and again in an hour. Work out how many pips each one moved.
